newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - HK stocks to make modest gains 1997.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - HK stocks to make modest gains 1997.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are likely to make modest gains this year, the Royal Bank of Canada said on Wednesday.

After outperforming other Asian centres last year and with the blue-chip Hang Seng Index rising more than 80 percent from its early 1995 lows, the local stock market gains are likely to be more modest in 1997, the bank said in a statement.
"The market has been driven by an economic rebound, as real GDP (gross domestic product) growth bottomed out in early 1996, and it has since risen steadily," it said.
"GDP growth is estimated at 4.4 percent in 1996 and 4.9 percent in 1997," it added.
Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said last week he expected GDP to grow by 5.5 percent in 1997 from 4.7 percent in 1996. The GDP growth rate was 4.6 percent in 1995.
"Property transactions and prices have both risen sharply, consumer spending is increasing, and corporate earnings have been steadily revised upward," the bank said.

"The property market's recovery is a signal of improving sentiment towards reunification with China in July, and an expected recovery in the Chinese economy should also benefit Hong Kong. Interest rates should continue to ease," it said.
"Despite these positives, the market looks close to fully valued and the political risk remains, with foreign investors likely to be cautious before July 1," the bank said.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China on July 1.
